ideas.label: Opposite Bishops (Ending)
ideas.summary: With opposite-colored bishops, the side with the initiative should attack on the color complex the opponent cannot defend. Extra pawns or a safer king often matter more than exact material equality.
games: Alexander Alekhine vs Jose Raul Capablanca 1927 (E16) [bookwalk]
source_books: Small Steps to Giant Improvement: Master Pawn Play in Chess

ideas.label: Opposite Bishops (Ending)
ideas.summary: The defender should place pawns on the color of their bishop, blockade passed pawns on the enemy bishop's color, and trade into a pure opposite-bishop ending when the attacker cannot create a second front.
games: Alexander Alekhine vs Jose Raul Capablanca 1927 (E16) [bookwalk]
source_books: Small Steps to Giant Improvement: Master Pawn Play in Chess

ideas.label: Opposite Bishops (Ending)
ideas.summary: To win opposite-bishop middlegames, combine kingside pressure with a queenside passer or a second weakness. One fixed target is often enough for a draw; two distant problems overwhelm the defending bishop.
games: Alexander Alekhine vs Jose Raul Capablanca 1927 (E16) [bookwalk]
source_books: Small Steps to Giant Improvement: Master Pawn Play in Chess
